title: A check-in that waits on CI waits at most 55 minutes, read from one dated constant
why: A wake past the prompt cache lifetime pays to reload the whole context.
source: plan restart-plan (main), coordinator 11:46 CST Nov 12 for lane ruling-parts-cite-steps; R32 part 3 (owner pick c, Nov 11)
note: Rule git-ci-wait-checks-in ("each wider apart") becomes "each wider apart, never past 55 minutes". The cap is read from one constant that names its source and date (the prompt cache lifetime), so a change reaches every caller at once and the claim can be re-checked when it goes stale (owner: "we should keep some sort of tabs on how anthropic determiines warm cash so this doesn't go stale"). Ready, no lane. Lane ci-wait-cap-55 started 11:48 CST Nov 12 (coordinator): first checks the 55 against R3 (a total-time limit is read from green runs, never a stored number; step time-limits-end-hangs-only) and brings the coordinator any clash before building. Coordinator pick a 11:50 CST Nov 12: the 55 is a dated cache fact, not an R3 time limit, so the step builds as written. #2839 reopened after batch 104 merged (bcbeaa26a, 14:43 CST Nov 12); rebase on main and re-run lane-lint.
